top_action: Prune and remove all heavily infected, spotted, and dying leaves. Dispose of them by burning or deep burial to reduce the inoculum load.

farmer.summary: The farmer's maize crop is exhibiting brown spots and wilting in hot weather.

diagnosis: Gray Leaf Spot (GLS) progressing to stalk rot, or Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND). The brown spots indicate severe foliar infection, while the wilting suggests vascular damage, stalk rot, or extreme plant stress.
top_action: Spray a broad-spectrum systemic and contact fungicide to halt the spread of the fungal pathogen.

farmer.summary: A farmer in Kisumu reports that their maize leaves are turning yellow.

diagnosis: Nitrogen deficiency exacerbated by moisture stress. High temperatures and low humidity are causing rapid soil moisture loss, locking up nitrogen in the soil and preventing root absorption, which leads to yellowing leaves (chlorosis) starting from the older lower leaves.
top_action: Top-dress with CAN (Calcium Ammonium Nitrate) fertilizer to replenish soil nitrogen. Apply carefully in the band near the plant base rather than broadcasting to minimize wind drift.

Crop: Maize
Issue: Nitrogen deficiency exacerbated by moisture stress. High temperatures and low humidity are causing rapid soil moisture loss, locking up nitrogen in the soil and preventing root absorption, which leads to yellowing leaves (chlorosis) starting from the older lower leaves.
Action: Top-dress with CAN (Calcium Ammonium Nitrate) fertilizer to replenish soil nitrogen. Apply carefully in the band near the plant base rather than broadcasting to minimize wind drift.
When: Apply early morning or late evening when wind speed drops below 5 m/s to prevent fertilizer drift.
Cost: KES 4,500 for 1 to 2 bags (50kg) of MEA CAN per acre
Follow up in 3 days.
